value.rationale: The random genus-g reflective-semigroup model is canonical because there is one semigroup per admissible multiplicity. A local gap invariant has a universal discrete heavy-tail limit 1/[k(k+1)] with infinite mean, while the exact finite population means grow logarithmically with g. The exact histogram gives a natural complete fixed-genus classification, connects it to divisor summatory arithmetic, quantifies convergence uniformly in all k with a matching lower-bound scale, and identifies a genuine extreme multiplicity-two effect. These are structural statements across all genera, not arbitrary small finite computations.
